# Procedural Regulations
The following regulations are enforced by specific points of Standard Operating Procedure. Please refer to Article 3 for further context on how these should be enforced.
## NanoTrasen Building & Expansion Regulations
In order to ensure that all parts of the station are up to NanoTrasen's safety and quality standards, all new constructions must follow a certain set of requirements.
Requirements for any new construction are as follows: - In order to maintain NanoTrasen's dignity and public image, any new constructions must not be excessively unsightly, or otherwise go against NanoTrasen's best interests. - Any part of the construction must not obstruct or impede any existing departmental functions and duties. - The construction must not impede or block any public thoroughfares. Sufficient measures should be made to ensure that any installations placed in a hallway still have safe and unobstructed routes around it. - Any new construction must not require an excessive or unattainable amount of resources, relative to the station’s current needs. - For constructions requiring power, extensions to the power grid must be done safely, according to local station standards. - Enclosed rooms that will house live inhabitants require proper and safe connections to the local Atmospherics system, including a Fire Alarm, Firelocks, Distribution, and Waste Lines.
## NanoTrasen Cleanliness Regulations
In order to maintain a safe and efficient working environment, as well as to maintain NanoTrasen's dignity and public image, ALL crew on duty are required to adhere to certain cleanliness standards.
Efforts should be made to either fulfill these standards by hand, or by calling a Janitor to clean in their stead. Failure to attend to a mess within 10 minutes may result in Corporate Misconduct actions.
Basic cleanliness expectations are as follows: - Corridors between workspaces kept free of debris, blockages, and potential slipping hazards, in order to maintain an efficient flow between departments. - Ample lighting should be present in any room outside of maintenance. In any working environment, color and brightness should be kept appropriate for that department. - Public-facing rooms should be kept pristine: Free of trash, improperly stored equipment, and other unsightly items that may damage NanoTrasen's public image. - Departmental staff in uniform and in sight of the public must make efforts to maintain the cleanliness of their appearance, such as regularly washing their uniforms. - In order to prevent attracting unwanted pests, unsealed and perishable food and drink should not be left unattended. Sighted pests should be dealt with and disposed of posthaste.
Certain locations are held to higher standards in terms of cleanliness. These locations include: - Any room that represents NanoTrasen's dignity and authority, such as the bridge or court. - Any room where patients are treated. - Any room where food and drink is consumed. - Any room with potentially hazardous and/or highly reactive substances. - Any room that stores weaponry.
## Corporate Misconduct & Disciplinary Actions
A member of Command may issue Disciplinary Actions to any of their subordinates that commit acts of Corporate Misconduct. If Corporate Misconduct is observed by a member of Internal Affairs, they are to immediately bring it to the attention of the relevant head of staff. Examples Include: - An Internal Affairs Agent notices the Misconduct during an Audit. - The Magistrate notices that a charge they are judging for falls under a Misconduct. - The Executive Officer notices on all-comms that a Misconduct is occurring.
A member of Internal Affairs can never issue a Disciplinary Action regarding Corporate Misconduct on their own. It always requires signing off by either the relevant Head of Staff, or the Captain. Internal Affairs should recommend a severity level based on the Misconduct, but the final severity is always up to the signee.
### Corporate Misconduct Categories
Corporate Misconduct
Description
Example
Insubordination
Going against a direct order from your departmental superiors.
Activating the SM after the CE told you not to.
SOP Violation
Egregiously going against the guidelines set by your job's Standard Operating Procedures.
See Article 3, Standard Operating Procedure.
Theft of Departmental Property
Taking equipment or products from your department without permission or proper payment.
Taking topicals from a Medkit and giving it to an Assistant for free.
Damage to Assigned Company Equipment
Intentionally or recklessly damaging your job's assigned equipment.
Placing an APE next to an electric anomaly, resulting in a discharge that destroys it.
Fraud
Performing your job's duties in a particularly deceptive or self-serving way.
Lying to certain crewmembers about the state of Science's research offerings.
Incompetence
Egregiously failing to meet assigned quotas, or performing your job's duties in a reckless or dangerous way.
Failing to perform an acceptable amount of your job's work this shift.
### Corporate Misconduct Disciplinary Actions
Class I
Confiscation
Class IV
Demotion
Class V
Contract Termination
### Corporate Honesty & Loyalty Incentive Policy Should a crew member be forthright with their Misconduct, and turn themselves in, consider reducing the severity of their Disciplinary Action as a reward for their honesty.
If a crew member that witnesses a Corporate Misconduct reports it to Internal Affairs before the perpetrator does, that crew member shall receive a reward for their loyalty.
